title: "Open Weights"
description: "A model release that makes learned parameter values available, without necessarily making the full system open source."
term: "Open Weights"
letter: "O"

difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

When a model has open weights, people can download its learned parameters
and run or adapt them under the release's terms. This does not by itself
mean that the training data, code, or full development process are public.

## Technical explanation

Model weights are the learned numerical parameters of a trained model.
Releasing them can enable local inference, fine-tuning, and independent
evaluation, depending on the model architecture, tooling, compute needs,
and license. The phrase "open weights" describes availability of
parameters, not necessarily every component of the model lifecycle.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Available weights can support deployment control, customization, and
research access. Engineers still need to assess license restrictions,
provenance, safety, data handling, model quality, and the compute required
to operate the model.

## How it works

A publisher distributes parameter files and usually specifies the
architecture, tokenizer, configuration, and terms of use. A compatible
runtime loads these files and executes the model. Reproducibility may still
be limited if training data, code, or training details are unavailable.

## Practical example

A company might download an open-weight language model, run inference in
its own environment, and fine-tune it for a domain. It must first check the
license and verify performance, security, and resource requirements for its
intended use.

## Common misconceptions

- Open weights are not synonymous with open source; released weights alone may not satisfy an open-source definition.
- Availability of weights does not reveal the full training dataset or guarantee reproducibility.
- Downloadable weights do not remove licensing, safety, or deployment obligations.
